message:
Centralized midspan beats distributed units for this single-mode bridge, Manager.

In plain words both masses where motion is largest give full push per kilogram while units moved off centre do less work and need more steel and more access stops. I keep the twin Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Tuned Mass Damper (TMD), pair on one cross-beam at midspan because off-centre effectiveness falls to 0.750 from the modal-effectiveness calculation (E67), so spreading needs about one third more moving mass, while detuning plus or minus 5 percent still holds 0.476 to 0.526 metres per second squared from the detuning sweep (E70).

Below-deck clearance is set by sag plus shake with nothing outside girder depth, Bridge Retrofit Engineer.

In plain words the soft spring stretches under its own weight more than it shakes and that total drop plus cage must stay above the bottom flange with nothing on deck. Static sag 74.7 mm from the static-sag calculation (E63) plus peak travel 49.4 mm from the free-decay simulation (E17) sums to 124 mm total from the envelope calculation (E68), about a hand length and well below a door width or person height, which fits inside girder depth as shown in the twin under-deck layout sketch (E55) with High-Strength Friction-Grip, defined as High-Strength Friction-Grip (HSFG), clamped cross-beam above the flange line.

Access is from below in one setup with no deck opening, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor.

In plain words tuning and lock pins must be reachable without cutting the walkway because any deck hatch breaks the no-visible-change commitment. I take from the Bridge Design Manual Section 2 — 2026 (E49) the Below Bridge Access Vehicle, defined as Below Bridge Access Vehicle (BBAV), inspection-access rule, which from my discipline means service by BBAV with caged lock pins and annual tune check and no deck hatch, and I confirm what you take from the Millennium Bridge, London (E39) that silhouette is kept by working under deck, but I qualify it because that 37 viscous plus 52 tuned-mass spread covered multiple lateral and vertical modes while this 1.9 Hz vertical mode needs only the centralized pair; stop hit 8.40 kN from the stop-force calculation (E66) sits inside combined 13.1 kN demand from the combined-load calculation (E65), about seventeen body weights and everyday liftable scale, against 32.9 kN slip per bolt from the slip-resistance calculation (E64).

My position is ready, because clearance, single-setup from-below access and centralized-pair choice close my domain with buildable clamped steel and measured Medium comfort proof.
